name: Reservoir Sampling
tagline: Selecting a uniform random sample of k items from an unbounded stream of unknown length n in one pass and O(k) memory.
purpose: Build a progressive mental model of reservoir sampling—from Vitter's Algorithm R and $O(k(1 + \log(n/k)))$ Algorithm L skips to weighted Efraimidis-Spirakis and distributed min-heap merges.

spark.summary: Reservoir sampling selects a uniformly random sample of k items from a data stream of unknown or unbounded length n in a single pass using O(k) memory.

spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** **Reservoir sampling** solves a core streaming constraint: picking $k$ items uniformly at random from a stream of unknown length $n$ in **one pass** and **$O(k)$ RAM**.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Single-Pass O(k) Reservoir Updates on Stream A, B, C, D, E (Event Stream -> PRNG j in [1..i] -> Reservoir[0..2]); Per-Shard Min-Heap -> Global Top-K Priority Merge (Global Top-K Heap -> Shard 1 (1M ev/m) -> Shard 2 (10k ev/m) -> Key = log(u)/w).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Compare CPU cost, memory predictability, and distributed mergeability. Each of 16 Kafka consumer workers runs a local $O(k)$ min-heap keyed by `u = rng.random()` (or `log(u)/w`).

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore randomized algorithms, tail-based APM sampling, and streaming pipelines.

learningJourney.title: What is Reservoir Sampling (Algorithm R & Algorithm L)

explanation.foundation: **Reservoir sampling** solves a core streaming constraint: picking $k$ items uniformly at random from a stream of unknown length $n$ in **one pass** and **$O(k)$ RAM**.
explanation.core: In **Vitter's Algorithm R**, you store the first $k$ items, then for each $i > k$ (1-indexed), draw random $j \in [1, i]$; if $j \le k$, overwrite `reservoir[j-1]`. By induction, every item has exact probability $k/n$. **Algorithm L** speeds this up from $O(n)$ to $O(k(1 + \log(n/k)))$ by sampling geometric skip distances.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of Reservoir Sampling, watch how what is reservoir sampling (algorithm r & algorithm l) interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. Reservoir sampling selects a uniformly random sample of k items from a data stream of unknown or unbounded length n in a single pass using O(k) memory.

learningJourney.title: Why we need Reservoir Sampling (and Distributed Merge Traps)

explanation.foundation: Think of **Why we need Reservoir Sampling (and Distributed Merge Traps)** as the intuition layer for Reservoir Sampling: The problem: see what breaks without Reservoir Sampling under real concurrency or scale.
explanation.core: Telemetry agents, Kafka consumers, and `PostgreSQL ANALYZE` cannot buffer billions of rows or run two passes. Two subtle traps break naive implementations: (1) **Biased Distributed Merge**: concatenating $k$ items from a 1M-event shard and a 10k-event shard over-represents the quiet shard by 100x; (2) **Stale History**: in an infinite daemon, after 10B events, new items have $k/10^{10}$ entry probability unless tumbled or time-decayed.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, why we need reservoir sampling (and distributed merge traps) becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. decisionFramework.decision: To keep storage layouts predictable as data grows, maintain a fixed k-element array and accept the i-th incoming item (i > k) with probability k/i, replacing a random slot—giving every item an exact k/n selection probability without knowing n upfront.
